label: copy phase: just-copied w with m to output next (w->m bigram recall)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost only when the fed-back input is w (96.5% of activation mass; input m gives the other 3.5%). It is strongest when the token to output next is m, meaning the original sequence had the bigram w m. Top activations are all of the form ... w m ... <DEL> ... [w], and the following m step often fires weakly too. Magnitude is highest for w->m at recall_idx 2-4. It is weaker but still present when m comes two outputs later (next_out == m), and it fires faintly on w inputs followed by other tokens. It is almost silent when w is the first original token (recall_idx 1), and it is smaller at the final output step. It never fires in the original or delimiter phases. The predicate (input w, output m, recall_idx >= 2) gets precision 0.84 and mass recall 0.72 on dev, but recall is only 0.49 because of the many weak activations on w followed by other tokens and on m->m.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=w (+8.53), phase=2 & in_tok=m (+4.36), next_out=m (+4.30), phase=2 & out_tok=m (+4.28), in_tok=w (+4.05), out_tok=m (+4.01). Lower it: recall_idx=1 (-2.74), prev_tok=<DEL> (-2.74), recall_idx=6 (-2.54), out_tok=n (-2.47).
